claims.text: The coatings consist of alternating layers of an HEA and another ceramic or metallic material.
Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation is governed by the interaction between the multilayer architecture and sluggish diffusion in the HEA.
Sluggish diffusion is an inherent characteristic of HEAs.
Reduced atomic mobility delays creep mechanisms.
Sustained mechanical stress at elevated temperature induces time-dependent plastic deformation in these coatings.
The relevant test conditions include temperatures of approximately 600–1000 °C under constant stress for an extended period.
Interfaces introduced by the multilayer structure act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The combination of interface barriers and reduced atomic mobility delays creep and other time-dependent deformation processes.
HEA multilayer coatings will have significantly lower time-dependent plastic-deformation rates than single-layer HEA coatings under identical conditions.
HEA multilayer coatings will have significantly lower time-dependent plastic-deformation rates than conventional non-HEA multilayer coatings under identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies where sluggish-diffusion effects remain significant, above room temperature and below the HEA melting point.
The proposed mechanism requires multilayer architectures with well-defined interfaces.
Layer thickness and composition may influence resistance to time-dependent deformation.
